content.title: Patterns in Mathematics
content.introduction: Patterns in Mathematics is developed as a reasoning journey in which learners notice Patterns in Mathematics, observation, reasoning, application, evidence. The Gurukul lesson moves from observation and representation to explanation, practice, checking and transfer. Learners are expected to show how they know, not only state an answer.

student_explanation.title: Patterns in Mathematics
student_explanation.opening: Patterns in Mathematics is developed as a reasoning journey in which learners notice Patterns in Mathematics, observation, reasoning, application, evidence. The Gurukul lesson moves from observation and representation to explanation, practice, checking and transfer. Learners are expected to show how they know, not only state an answer.

sections.explanation: In this chapter, Patterns in Mathematics is useful because it helps us notice, explain or apply an important idea. Start with a familiar example, identify the evidence, and then explain the conclusion in your own words.
